summary: The Vibe Jam portal convention is a small informal rule set, published by the organiser of the Vibe Jam game competition, for linking browser games into a webring. A game may place an exit portal that sends the player to a Vibe Jam address, which forwards them to a randomly chosen participating game, and a game that receives a player places a return portal to the game they came from. The player's name, colour, speed, direction of travel, rotation, health, team and an avatar link ride along as optional values in the web address so the next game can place the player with continuity. It covers the hop itself and nothing else: there is no identity check, no agreed format for what the avatar link points to, no state beyond the listed values and no way to name a chosen destination, and everything about rendering, physics, sensing and capture is left to each game. Trap for a standards audience: it is a page of prose plus one sample script, not a versioned specification, all values travel unauthenticated in plain web addresses to whichever game comes next, and the sample return code navigates to whatever address the incoming ref value names.

coverage.note: The exit portal sends the player to a Vibe Jam address with their name, colour, speed, health, team, avatar link, velocity and rotation as optional values, and the receiving game uses them to place the player. The page defines only those listed values; the sample script starts from the current query values, so other values received also travel on.
